blocks.packageReason: legacy-closure-pending-request. Package for the effect only: opening a NAMED window (an entry-local flag in `tempSummonData.abilityEntryWindows` that resets on switch, plus the per-wave 'already opened' memory) has no library effect (R-B12-15) and the window has no reading atom (R-B12-16: `time.in-entry-window{key}`). 1 attr: Forewarn (108 attr 1, key 'upgrade:forewarn:two-turn-soothsayer', the shipped upgrade that gives Forewarn a two-turn Soothsayer; attr 0 is EntryEffectAbAttr, attr 2 TimeLimitedEffectivenessFloorAbAttr). The gate is `canApply` moved into `gate` (Tier B split, pure move of code). Its natural library form is time.once-per { wave, key }, which reads and writes the same Set (`waveData.entryEffectsFired`), BUT the carrier writes the key right BEFORE this class's `apply` runs, and `apply` returns early when the key is already present, so the window would never open (a test in B12/chunk2.test.ts proves it). So the user's gate stays a legacy-closure until the library offers either the window effect (R-B12-15) or a once-per whose write waits until after the effect. Oddities, not fixed: (a) the name says 'once per battle' but the memory is `waveData`, which is reset every wave, so the window opens once per WAVE; (b) `apply` re-tests the key although the dispatcher already ran `canApply`, which is harmless but is what makes the library atom unusable; (c) a simulated call neither opens the window nor remembers the key.

blocks.packageReason: Package for the effect only, justified: the library's stat-stage effect has a fixed stat chosen by staff (one stat, one number of stages), and the library has no 'foe's highest stat of this group' choice; the stat is picked from the foe's live values at the moment of the effect, so it cannot be a fixed block (request R-B12-14: `effect.stat-stage` with `stat: highest-of-group`, target 'each foe next to me'). The effect still has a typed setting (the rule list, with a codec) and the trigger is the swappable shared WHEN `event.on-entry`; there is no condition inside. Tier C, 1 attr: Malicious (5305 attr 0): rules [Attack or Sp. Atk, -1] then [Defense or Sp. Def, -1] (read from the live attr). Oddities, not fixed: (0) the dispatcher comment and the archetype file header say 'the higher of Attack vs Defense and of Sp. Atk vs Sp. Def', but the live rules compare Attack with Sp. Atk and Defense with Sp. Def, which matches the ability text 'highest Attack and Defense stat'; (a) `canApply` counts ALL opponents (`getOpponents`) while `apply` walks only the adjacent ones, so in a triple battle with only a far foe the ability flashes and does nothing; (b) `apply` has no random draw but queues one phase per rule per foe, so the order of the rules is the order of the drops; (c) a tie between two candidates keeps the first listed because the comparison is strictly greater than; (d) the highest stat is measured without stat stages, so a foe whose Defense was raised by stages can still lose its (higher by base value) Attack.
